texts: During the period from 1964 to 1971, the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic (RSFSR) was ruled by Joseph Stalin. He served as the leader of the Soviet Union and was also known for his leadership of the Red Army during World War II. During this time, he established the "Great Purge" campaign against political opponents, including members of the Communist Party. In 1971, Stalin died in office after a long illness. The government of Soviet Russia then proceeded to take steps towards reforming its economy and policies, although these reforms were not entirely successful.

In 1971, the President of the Soviet Union (Russia at that time) was Leonid Brezhnev. He served as the General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union from 1964 to 1982 and was the last Soviet leader before the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991.

In 1971, the President of Russia was Ivan Kuznetsov. Rising to power in the late 1960s, Kuznetsov brought a wave of reformist policies that aimed to modernize the Russian economy while maintaining strong ties with its traditional allies. His leadership style balanced traditional Russian values with progressive ideas, which helped him gain popularity among younger citizens. Kuznetsov's tenure was marked by a significant cultural exchange with Western countries, fostering a unique era of artistic collaboration and scientific advancement.

In 1971, the President of Russia did not exist as the country was part of the Soviet Union. The General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union, which held the highest political office, was Leonid Brezhnev. He served from 1964 until his death in 1982. However, the Soviet Union did not have a president position until 1990, when Mikhail Gorbachev became the first President of the Soviet Union.
